paper_title: OctoTools: A Multi-Agent Framework with Extensible Tools for Complex Reasoning
hook: Can one AI system count objects in an image, crack a math puzzle, and answer medical board questions, all without a single step of extra training? A team at Stanford says yes, and their answer has eight arms.
problem: Complex reasoning means juggling vision, calculation, knowledge lookup, and multi-step logic all at once. Language models can borrow external tools for this, but existing frameworks demand costly training data, stay locked to one narrow domain, or fall apart when a problem takes many steps.
method: OctoTools fixes this with three ideas working together. Tool cards wrap every tool in standardized metadata, so a new tool plugs in with no retraining and no framework changes. A planner agent drafts a high-level plan, then at each step picks one sub-goal and one tool. An executor agent translates that action into runnable Python and executes it. After every step, a context verifier decides: keep going, or stop and let the summarizer compile the answer.
experiments: The Stanford team stress-tested this on sixteen benchmarks spanning vision, math, science, medicine, and agentic tasks, then went further, pitting OctoTools against AutoGen, GPT-Functions, and LangChain with the same GPT-4o backbone, identical tools, and the same ten-step budget.
results: OctoTools averaged 58.5 percent accuracy, 9.3 points above GPT-4o alone and up to 10.6 points above rival frameworks holding the very same tools. The gains were largest where tools matter most: over 22 points on the Game of 24 math puzzle and on pathology image classification.
contribution: A training-free, extensible multi-agent framework for complex reasoning
Planner-executor paradigm with standardized tool cards
Greedy toolset optimization, validated across 16 benchmarks
insight: Here is the deeper lesson: when the team dissected 200 failures, 65 percent traced to weak tools and barely one percent to the framework itself. Separating planning from execution is what keeps an agent reliable.
takeaway: Smarter agents are not just bigger models. They are better-organized ones. That is OctoTools.
